title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page holds one short paragraph, crossed out with diagonal strokes. It reads approximately: 'Supposons qu'on ait S = Spec F_q [or F_{p^ν}]. Alors on peut définir F_X^{(ν)}, qui est un S-endomorphisme [...], et qui agit donc sur ω.'

It is an abandoned first draft of the remark completed on the previous page. Take X/S smooth (and proper) of relative dimension 1, and let ω = f_*Ω^1_{X/S}. When S is the spectrum of a finite field F_{p^ν}, the relative ν-fold Frobenius F^{(ν)}_{X/S}: X → X^{(p^ν/S)} composed with the canonical identification X^{(p^ν/S)} ≅ X (valid because F_S^ν = id_S) gives an S-endomorphism of X. It coincides with the absolute iterate F_X^ν.

Being an S-endomorphism, it acts on ω. More precisely, through the trace/Cartier map F^{(ν)}_* = Tr it gives an endomorphism of ω. On the next page this endomorphism is identified with the transpose of F^* on R^1f_*O. That page then uses it to compare the eigenvalues of the Cartier operator on ω (equivalently the Hasse–Witt matrix) with the unit-root eigenvalues of ℓ-adic or crystalline Frobenius mod p, citing Katz.

The point served is the classical link between the Cartier operator on regular differentials, the Hasse–Witt matrix, and Frobenius eigenvalues over finite fields. Grothendieck crossed this out and replaced it with the more general formulation on the preceding page (arbitrary S, with the hypothesis that λ ↦ λ^{p^ν} is the identity on O_S).
errors: No mathematical error. The statement is correct but incomplete, and it was abandoned: it was crossed out in favour of the more general version on the previous page.

ideas.what: Over S = Spec F_q, the iterated relative Frobenius is an S-endomorphism of X (equal to F_X^ν) and therefore acts on ω = f_*Ω^1_{X/S}, e.g. via the Cartier/trace map.
ideas.modern_name: q-Frobenius endomorphism of a variety over F_q; Cartier operator on H^0(X, Ω^1)
ideas.where_published: Frobenius formalism in SGA 5 (Exp. XV, Frobenius and traces) and SGA 4½; standard in Katz's work on Hasse–Witt and Gauss–Manin

deep.surprise_reason: This is a crossed-out, routine draft sentence about the Frobenius acting on differentials over a finite field. Its content is standard and is superseded on the neighbouring pages.
transcription_corrections: The superscript in 'F_X^{(?)}' appears to be '(ν)', i.e. F_X^{(ν)}.
The base field is likely 'S = Spec F_q' (possibly F_{p^ν}) rather than 'Spec F_p'. With F_p, ν would be superfluous.
The whole paragraph is struck through with diagonal lines; it is a deleted draft.
The line ends with an underlined 'et' after the S-endomorphism clause, leading into 'qui agit donc sur ω' (ω underlined).
